Research Foundations

Source: vignettes/rx-foundations.Rmd
rx-foundations.Rmd

Below is a selected bibliography of research relevant to defining and analyzing treatment episodes in longitudinal behavioral health data. The literature is organized around two related methodological issues: how distinct episodes of care have been identified in longitudinal treatment records and how treatment outcomes have been analyzed when individuals contribute repeated episodes of care.

Time-based episode definitions

A large number of intervention studies have used the time between treatment contacts to distinguish separate episodes of behavioral health care. In psychotherapy research, a gap of at least 90 days without treatment has frequently been used to identify the beginning of a new episode of care. This approach provides a practical and clinically interpretable rule for distinguishing relatively short interruptions in ongoing treatment from subsequent reengagement.

Importantly, many studies using time-based episode definitions have not subsequently analyzed all identified episodes. Instead, episode delimiters have often been used to identify distinct periods of care before selecting a single episode—such as the first or most recent episode—for the primary analysis. These studies nevertheless provide important methodological precedent for treating sufficiently long gaps between sessions as evidence of distinct treatment episodes.

  1. Goldberg, S. B., Rousmaniere, T., Miller, S. D., Whipple, J., Nielsen, S. L., Hoyt, W. T., & Wampold, B. E. (2016). Do psychotherapists improve with time and experience?   2. Minami, T., Davies, D. R., Tierney, S. C., Bettmann, J. E., McAward, S. M., Averill, L. A., Huebner, L. A., Weitzman, L. M., Benbrook, A. R., Serlin, R. C., & Wampold, B. E. (2009).   5. Kilcullen, J., Castonguay, L. G., Janis, R. A., Hallquist, M. N., Hayes, J. A., & Locke, B. D. (2021). Predicting future courses of psychotherapy within a grouped LASSO framework. Psychotherapy Research, 31(1), 63–77. https://doi.org/10.1080/10503307.2020.1762948

Analysis of Repeated Episodes

A separate body of research has examined clients who engage in more than one episode of treatment. Definitions of an episode vary considerably across this literature, and many studies rely on retrospective reports of previous treatment experiences rather than longitudinal records of care. Consequently, although repeated treatment utilization has received substantial attention, relatively few studies have identified and analyzed multiple episodes of care for the same clients within a single longitudinal data set.

  1. Kilcullen, J., Castonguay, L. G., Janis, R. A., Hallquist, M. N., Hayes, J. A., & Locke, B. D. (2021). Predicting future courses of psychotherapy within a grouped LASSO framework. Psychotherapy Research, 31(1), 63–77. https://doi.org/10.1080/10503307.2020.1762948
